comments.value:
The growing number of AI-generated or AI "enhanced" world thumbnails has really made world hopping a lot less fun for me.

I've been trying not to let it get to me because there are plenty of world authors in the past where I've said "there's no way that's what it looks like" and been totally blown away by what they've been able to accomplish.

But now when I see something that looks like it might be impressive my first thought is something like "do I even want to bother to find out".

It feels like I'm constantly wading through attempts to deceive me
Require content to declare it and give us a filter to filter it out, thank yoooou

I dont care much about it being used in group banners, but the one thing that does bother me is AI generated world thumbnails that are clearly meant to depict the world itself and are therefore misleading to whats actually in the world.

I agree, it should be reguired to declare through a world tag and users should be able to filter out that tag in world searches or in the default world tabs (Popular, Newly Updated, etc...). I've been wanting to be ablw to hide them for some time so they dont show up when I'm looking for new worlds.
I support this idea and want it implemented. But also I really don't want witchhunts to be a thing. I've had my share of unfounded AI accusations and it hurts when you're wrongly called AI.
Please give us this. ai generated assets lag my machine so bad. I don't like wandering into that stuff blindly

Despite what 'leading' 'tech' 'experts' saying to the contrary, the technology is not meant for asset generation. Hallucinations, overcomplications, inefficient topography, and so on leads to massive, unoptimized 3D assets, and ugly urine-filtered textures.

If the blatant world-wide plagiarism isn't enough to make you wince, then the incompetence of the process must be taken very seriously. Hold the creators accountable for their unoptimized shortcuts.

GenAI content has no place in a creative space. It is literally the opposite of creativity, and if it goes unchecked and undeclared it undermines the very concept of genuine user creativity.

VRchat would not be the vibrant, diverse, creative space that it is if it were populated with GenAI slop at the start, and there is still absolutely no place for it now.

At the very least, VRchat should make this declaration mandatory, and discovery of a world publishing without doing so should be grounds for reporting it to VRchat moderation for mandatory adding of the genAI flag regardless of the creators wish to hide this fact.

If you must let genAI speak for itself, make it speak apart from genuine creativity, so that the clear indication of what users prefer in the worlds they choose not only to spend the finite time they have for VR, but the finite time they have with friends to make new memories in VR.

I'm so sick of the slop everywhere in real life let alone virtually, seconding this. VRChat at it's core is a creative community and GenAI is the antithesis. I'm not even asking for a full ban I wanna be able to avoid it just like I do on Steam with it's required disclosures.

I'm sick of slop, and normally I don't make an unconstructive emotionally driven reply on a post on canny since it contributes very little. But this is where i break my rule.

I'm sick of it. Its a cancer.
The uprise of AI in VRChat makes me not only not want to come back to it, but to actually actively boycott it.
@{5a565acbb301553d0104ba88|full_name} honestly I'm already refusing to give them anymore money until they give us SOMETHING. Even just liking/disliking or comments on worlds would help.

details: Content that uses generative AI should have to declare that it is being used, and should be able to be filtered out of search results and recommendations by the user.
title: Require content using generative AI to declare it
